Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

motivate verb

also motivated, motivating, spur, drive (someone to do something), prompt

classical

Cic. de Or. 1.126 (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Brut. 19: impulsī atque incēnsī (Lewis & Short)

impellō, impellere, impulī, impulsum

verb, third conjugation, transitive: aliquem ad aliquid, in aliquid, or ut + subjunctive

drive, induce (someone to do something)

Literally to push or strike; of the mind, the usual word in good prose for what moves someone to act (Lewis & Short). The reason is the subject: quae rēs tē ad hoc impulit?, what made you do this?

Other words

  • incitō, incitāre, incitāvī, incitātum — spur on, rouse

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Div. 2.5 (Lewis & Short); Cic. Brut. 317: imitandī cupiditāte (Lewis & Short)

    Literally to set in rapid motion (horses, ships); of people and their zeal, to stir up and spur on.

  • concitō, concitāre, concitāvī, concitātum — rouse, stir up, spur on

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 348

Examples

  • ad quam quemque artem putābat esse aptum, ad eam impellere atque hortārī solēbat

    whatever art he thought each of us was fitted for, he would drive and encourage us towards itCic. de Or. 1.126 (Lewis & Short)

  • quōrum studiō legendī meum scrībendī studium in diēs incitātur

    whose eagerness to read spurs on my eagerness to write from day to dayCic. Div. 2.5 (Lewis & Short)

See also encourage, encourage.

SourcesLewis & Short: impello · Lewis & Short: incito · Lewis & Short: concito
